subject: 2026-11-08-project-onboarding

errors: section `## Reasoning` is missing or empty

findings.title: Project docs reach the jury packs but can never ground a finding
quotes: appends `onboard.docs_for(root, "scope", slug)` to the scope lens's pack at the spec gate and `onboard.docs_for(root, "architecture-fit", slug)` to the architecture-fit lens's pack at the plan gate; other packs are unchanged.
files += [root / "CLAUDE.md"] + [root / n for n in dict.fromkeys(named)]
Files to read (quotes may come only from these):
findings.fix: extend CT-18 to bind `jury.sources` too: at the spec gate (scope) and plan gate (architecture-fit), add the project docs `docs_for` mapped for that reader and slug. They are then listed under "Files to read" and count for grounding. Add a TC where an architecture-fit finding quoting principles.md stays grounded.

sources.situation: The architecture-fit juror reads principles.md in its pack and raises "CT-n breaks principle X", quoting principles.md. `jury.grounding` checks quotes only against `jury.sources`, which lists the spec folder, CLAUDE.md and the bound/Like files, never `.nio/project/*.md`. So `add()` marks the finding ungrounded and drops it, and the pack header itself tells the juror it may not quote the docs. The same happens to a scope finding quoting product.md. The docs are delivered but cannot be used.

findings.reason: `jury.sources` (jury.py:200-214) lists only the spec folder, CLAUDE.md and the bound/Like files, and `grounding` reads only those. CT-18 appends `docs_for` to the pack text only and does not touch `sources`. A finding that quotes principles.md or product.md would therefore be marked ungrounded.
findings.note: grill Q29 (delegated session): jury.sources lists the docs the scope and architecture-fit lenses get, so their quotes ground (CT-18, CT-22, TC-55)

findings.title: US-6's scenario and tests need the onboard skill, which a later story delivers
quotes: ### US-6 Flag stale docs and reconcile them\n- Depends on: US-5\n- Delivers: CT-14

- Covers: CT-13
findings.fix: either move US-2 before US-6 (US-6 depends on US-2), or rewrite QS-3's Needs to a setup that doesn't use the skill (docs written by hand plus `nio onboard confirm`, as QS-4 does) and move TC-42 to US-2's test list.

sources.situation: When US-6 is done, QS-3 (its scenario) cannot be run. It needs QS-1 finished, and QS-1 runs `/nio:onboard`, which is CT-13, delivered by US-2. US-2 comes after US-6 and depends on it. US-6's test list also holds TC-42, which runs `@nio:onboard` (Covers CT-13). The US-6 entry can't show what it delivers until US-2 is built.

findings.title: Only full specs can name apps; epic and lite efforts in a multi-app project lose their docs
quotes: `src/nio/templates/spec.md`'s front matter gains `apps: []
"template": "spec-epic"
When `onboard.progress(root)["apps"]` is not empty and the route is `full` or `epic`
with no slug, or a spec naming none, the `spec` and `scope` readers get every app and the others none
findings.fix: add `apps: []` to `spec-epic.md` and `spec-bugfix.md` too, and either check apps for lite as well, or state in CT-6/CT-9 what a lite spec's worker gets (for example, every app's worker docs).

sources.situation: Epic specs are created from `spec-epic.md`, which CT-6 leaves without `apps:`. Yet `check` demands apps for the epic route, so every epic spec in a multi-app project fails `nio check spec` unless someone adds the key by hand. Lite specs (`spec-bugfix.md`) never name apps. By CT-9's rule, a lite effort's worker pack in a multi-app project then gets no stack or principles docs at all. FR-28 says "each spec" names its apps.

findings.reason: CT-6 adds `apps:` only to `templates/spec.md`. `spec.py` maps the epic route to `spec-epic` and the lite route to `spec-bugfix`, and no template other than `spec.md` gets the key. `check` demands apps for `epic`, and CT-9 gives a spec that names no apps no stack or principles docs for the worker. FR-28 says "each spec".
findings.note: grill Q24 (delegated session): apps: [] in all three templates; the check applies on every route to a spec with the key; older specs exempt; none named means every app (CT-6, CT-9)

findings.title: CT-18 adds the docs differently from what architecture.md settles
quotes: call `pack.build` with their reader and slug, so they carry the project docs too (FR-17)
appends `onboard.docs_for(root, "scope", slug)` to the scope lens's pack
findings.fix: keep CT-18 and correct architecture.md through a change request, so it says the jury packs append `onboard.docs_for` and only the worker pack goes through `pack.build`.

sources.situation: architecture.md, which is read-only to the plan, says the scope and architecture-fit packs call `pack.build` with a reader. CT-18 appends `docs_for` straight into `_pack_text`. Today `_pack_text` calls `memory.build` only for the consistency lens. CT-18's route is the sensible one, since calling `pack.build` would also add memory records to those packs, but it contradicts the approved note.

findings.note: architecture.md now says the lens packs append onboard.docs_for and only the worker pack uses pack.build (C-261108-unxo)

findings.title: `HEADINGS` has nothing to check for personas.md
quotes: personas: one `### P-1 <name>` entry with `Who`, `Wants`, `Allowed to`, `How often` lines
`HEADINGS` maps each doc to its `## ` headings, read by `confirm` (CT-4).
findings.fix: state in CT-12 what `confirm` checks for personas (at least one `### P-<n>` entry, each holding the four lines), and add that case to TC-6.

sources.situation: The personas template has no `## ` headings, only a `### P-1` entry with `Who`/`Wants`/`Allowed to`/`How often` lines. So `HEADINGS["personas"]` is empty or undefined. `nio onboard confirm personas` then accepts any personas.md, even one with no P-n entry, and TC-6's "every heading `onboard.HEADINGS[<doc>]` lists" passes without checking anything for personas.

findings.note: CT-12 check_doc: personas need a ### P-<n> entry with Who/Wants/Allowed to/How often lines; TC-6 asserts it

findings.title: Reconcile can never report "nothing to reconcile" when a scan file has no source record
quotes: the scan's files no doc records yet
IF reconcile finds no changed, new or deleted file THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL report that there is nothing to reconcile and change nothing.
findings.fix: make "new" mean a scan file outside the secrets category whose path no project doc has ever recorded. Let the onboarding grill record every non-secrets file it reviewed, even one that yielded no fact, for example in `onboarding.json`. Otherwise reconcile has nothing to compare against.

sources.situation: a freshly onboarded repo has a `.env` (secrets entry, path only, hash `""`, never read, so never recorded in any doc). It may also have a README the grill judged to hold no fact, so no doc records it. CT-14 treats every scan file no doc records as a file to review. Nothing changed since onboarding, yet reconcile finds a "new" file on every run. FR-22 and AC-25 say it must report nothing to reconcile, and CT-14 gives the opposite outcome. A secrets file also cannot be recorded, because it has no hash and is never read, so the loop never ends.

findings.reason: CT-14 reviews "the scan's files no doc records yet". A secrets entry has hash `""`, is never read, and so is never recorded. FR-22 and AC-25 require "nothing to reconcile" when nothing changed or was added, which CT-14 cannot produce in a repo that has a `.env`.
findings.note: grill Q25 (delegated session): onboarding.json keeps seen; nio onboard changed lists changed, deleted and new files; reconcile ends with nio onboard reconciled (CT-3, CT-4, CT-11, CT-14, TC-54; C-261108-unxo)

findings.title: Empty repo: nothing creates the NEEDS CLARIFICATION docs for stack, architecture and infra
quotes: the docs to confirm, `product`, `personas`, `principles` when `empty` (FR-12), else all six
mark every field of stack.md, architecture.md and infra.md NEEDS CLARIFICATION
findings.fix: say which step writes the three template copies. For example, `start --empty` copies the CT-12 templates for the docs it does not grill. State that `confirm`'s last-doc transition requires them to exist.

sources.situation: in an empty repo, `expected` leaves out stack, architecture and infra. CT-4 `confirm` creates nothing, and CT-13 only says to write "the doc `next:` names". After the three docs are confirmed, state is `done`, yet no `.nio/project/stack.md`, `architecture.md` or `infra.md` exists. AC-13 requires those files to read NEEDS CLARIFICATION in every field. CT-9 will instead emit `missing: stack` for the plan and worker readers. CT-21 (FR-13) has no NEEDS CLARIFICATION fields to find, so the first full spec's grill never asks them.

findings.reason: With `empty`, CT-3's `expected` leaves out stack, architecture and infra. CT-4 `confirm` writes no doc, and CT-13 only writes the doc `next:` names. No contract step creates the three NEEDS CLARIFICATION files that FR-12 and AC-13 require.
findings.note: grill Q26 (delegated session): start --empty writes the three blank docs from their templates (CT-4, TC-56)

findings.title: CT-4 sends "ignore" cells to exit 0 and also to exit 1
quotes: confirm, pause or skip outside the states the table allows → exit 1 naming the state
`ignore` cells exit 0 and change nothing
findings.fix: limit the exit-1 sentence to the table's `reject` cells (start on `done`, skip on `done`). Say that a confirm outside `in progress` is `ignore`, exit 0.

sources.situation: `nio onboard pause` while `not started` is the table cell `dev stops`/`not started` = `ignore`. A second `nio onboard skip "x"` while `skipped` is `ignore`. Calling `nio onboard confirm product` while `paused` or `skipped` is `ignore`. CT-4's Fails line says exit 1 for each, and its State line says exit 0 and change nothing. The table has two kinds of non-transition, `ignore` and `reject`, and `reject` is exit 1 only on `done`. A test written from the table (exit 0) fails against the Fails line (exit 1), or the reverse.

findings.reason: CT-4's Fails line says "confirm, pause or skip outside the states the table allows → exit 1". Its State line says "`ignore` cells exit 0 and change nothing". The spec table (lines 231-235) has `ignore` cells for pause on `not started`, confirm on `paused`, and skip on `skipped`. Those cells fall under both sentences.
findings.note: grill Q26 (delegated session): ignore cells exit 0 and print ignored; only start and skip on done exit 1 (CT-4, TC-56)

findings.title: The secrets scan walks git-ignored dependency and build trees
quotes: plus, for the secrets check only, `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard`
findings.fix: bound the ignored-file pass, for example by excluding ignored directories (`--directory`) or well-known dependency directories. Alternatively, state in the spec that listing all of them is intended.

sources.situation: the second `ls-files` call returns every ignored file, including all of `node_modules/`, `.venv/` and `build/`. Packages there routinely hold `*.key`, `*.pem`, `credentials*`, `secrets.*` and `.env*` files. FR-24 says every matching name is listed under secrets, git-ignored or not. Scanning a normal JS or Python repo can therefore yield hundreds of secrets entries. That drowns the real ones (`.env`, `prod.tfvars`) and slows the scan. FR-3 and NFR-2 expect a quick, readable scan, and AC-28 expects "two secrets entries".

findings.reason: `git ls-files --others --ignored --exclude-standard` lists every ignored file, including `node_modules/` and `.venv/` contents, and CT-1 applies the secrets name match to all of them. FR-24 does say "git-ignored or not", but nothing bounds the pass, so large lists are possible.
findings.note: Delegated: the human gave the orchestrator standing authority to take the recommended option (2026-11-08). FR-24 says secrets names are listed git-ignored or not; bounding the pass would change the approved spec. Entries are paths only and never read.

findings.title: Build order uses contracts before the stories that deliver them
quotes: the spec skill builds its drafting pack with
and, after an effort, those `nio onboard changed <ref>` lists
findings.fix: move CT-16's pack step to US-5. Move CT-11 to US-6 or ahead of it, or add US-7 to US-6's dependencies.

sources.situation: US-4 delivers CT-16, whose spec skill calls `nio pack ... --reader spec`. The `--reader` flag is CT-10, which is delivered by US-5, a later story. US-6 delivers CT-14, whose steps run `nio onboard changed <ref>`. That command is CT-11, which is delivered by US-7, a later story. At the end of US-4 and at the end of US-6 the shipped skill text names a command or flag that does not exist yet. The `Depends on` chain (US-4 to US-5 to US-6 to US-7) never lets those stories pass their own e2e checks.

findings.note: build order now US-1, US-4, US-5, US-2, US-3, US-6, US-7; CT-16 in US-5, CT-11 in US-6

findings.title: A patched repo doc has no backup and its restore is never tested
quotes: offer a patch to a stale repo doc and apply it only on a yes
Candidates are `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` (tracked and untracked, not ignored)
Assert: after run one CONTRIBUTING.md bytes equal the original; after run two they differ and mention `pytest`
findings.fix: in CT-13 (and in CT-14, if reconcile ever patches repo docs), run `nio onboard backup <file>` before applying any patch to a repo file. Extend TC-9 or TC-42 to copy the backup back and assert the original bytes.

sources.situation: the dev says yes to a patch of an untracked `docs/DEPLOY.md` or README, and the patch is wrong. The original bytes are gone. Agent files get `nio onboard backup` first (CT-13: "before changing one run `nio onboard backup <file>`"), but repo-doc patches don't, and git can't help with an untracked file.

findings.reason: CT-13 runs `nio onboard backup` only for agent files. The patch to a stale repo doc has no backup step, and CT-1 candidates include untracked files that git cannot restore. TC-9 only checks that the bytes differ after a yes.
findings.note: grill Q27 (delegated session): nio onboard backup before every repo-file patch in onboard and reconcile; TC-9 asserts the backup (CT-13, CT-14)

findings.title: A torn or corrupt onboarding.json is undefined, and resetting it would overwrite confirmed docs
quotes: `progress(root) -> dict` reads `.nio/project/onboarding.json` (see the data model)
Written only by `nio onboard`, read by `onboard.py`.
write the doc from the template with only confirmed content
findings.fix: in CT-4, write onboarding.json to a temp file and `os.replace` it, as `flow.record` does. In CT-3, have a file that isn't valid JSON exit 1 and name the file, never read as `not started`. Add an integration test with a truncated onboarding.json.

sources.situation: `nio onboard confirm` dies partway through writing the file. If `progress` raises, every full or epic `nio new spec` fails through CT-5. If it falls back to the missing-file default, `next_doc` returns `product` again, `start` writes an empty `confirmed`, and the skill rewrites the already-confirmed product.md from the template. Unlike `flow.record`, the contract names no temp-file-and-rename write.

findings.reason: CT-3 and CT-4 define no write method for `onboarding.json` and no behaviour for invalid JSON. CT-3 gives only the missing-file default, so a torn file has no defined handling.
findings.note: grill Q28 (delegated session): onboarding.json written via temp file and os.replace; invalid JSON stops the commands naming the file (CT-3, CT-4, TC-53)

findings.title: Resuming onboarding can overwrite an existing doc with its template
quotes: for the doc `next:` names, read the files that feed it
a later start from `paused` or `skipped` keeps the saved `confirmed`, `empty` and `apps` and ignores new flags
findings.fix: in CT-13, say that when the `next:` doc already exists, the skill starts from that file's content (or backs it up) rather than from the template. Add an e2e assertion that the existing facts survive.

sources.situation: the dev skipped onboarding, and a full spec's grill then wrote dev answers into stack.md (CT-21). Or the dev paused halfway through a doc. A later `@nio:onboard` writes that doc again "from the template", and the existing content is lost without anyone being asked.

findings.note: grill Q27 (delegated session): an existing doc is resumed from its own text, not the template (CT-13)

findings.title: CT-17's keep-first rule and outside-repo refusal have no integration test
quotes: A second backup of the same file on the same day keeps the first copy and prints its path.
the file doesn't exist, or lies outside the repo → exit 1 naming it; nothing written.
findings.fix: add an integration test in `tests/test_onboard.py`. It backs up a file, changes it, backs it up again and asserts the backup still holds the original bytes. It also checks that a missing file and a path outside the repo both exit 1 with nothing written.

sources.situation: if an implementation overwrites the same-day backup on a second call, the only copy of the original is replaced by changed bytes. TC-18, the only test of CT-17, runs only with `NIO_E2E=1` and calls backup just once.

findings.note: TC-52 (misuse, integration) covers backup keep-first and refusals

findings.title: Specs written before `apps:` existed fail `nio check spec` in a multi-app project
quotes: When `onboard.progress(root)["apps"]` is not empty and the route is `full` or `epic`, `check` adds `spec names no app; the project has apps: <a>, <b>` when `apps` is empty
findings.fix: say in CT-6 how a spec created before onboarding is treated: either it is exempt, or the dev adds `apps:` through a change request. Add one TC for an old spec with no `apps` key.

sources.situation: a project with a full spec already in flight onboards with apps `web` and `api`. The old spec has no `apps` key, so `nio check spec` (and any gate that runs it) now fails on a spec that was already approved. The plan gives no backfill or grace rule.

findings.note: grill Q24 (delegated session): a spec without the apps key, written before this feature, is left as it is and its packs get every app (CT-6, CT-9)

findings.title: TC-42 runs the onboard skill a story before the skill is built
quotes: - Action: run @nio:onboard
- Delivers: CT-6, CT-13, CT-17
findings.fix: move TC-42 to US-2's Tests, or deliver CT-13 before US-6.

sources.situation: TC-42 is in US-6's build-order entry and runs @nio:onboard, but `skills/onboard/SKILL.md` (CT-13) is delivered by US-2, which "Depends on: US-6". The test can't pass inside its own entry, so US-6 can't close green. If someone makes it pass early by stubbing the skill, a missing rehash after a patch goes unnoticed.

findings.reason: The US-6 entry lists TC-42, which runs `@nio:onboard` (CT-13). CT-13 is delivered by US-2, and US-2 "Depends on: US-6". The test cannot pass inside its own story.
findings.note: TC-42 moved to US-2, which delivers the onboard skill

findings.title: TC-6 and TC-31 take their expected values from the code under test
quotes: each `.nio/project/<doc>.md` holds every heading `onboard.HEADINGS[<doc>]` lists
the `### ` doc headings in each pack equal `onboard.READERS[<r>]` (as `<doc>.md`), no more, no fewer
| worker | stack, principles | [human] |
findings.fix: write the expected heading lists from spec Key entities, and the expected reader-to-docs sets from the Docs per reader table, as literals in the tests.

sources.situation: if `HEADINGS["stack"]` leaves out `CI` (and the template it seeds leaves it out too), or `READERS["worker"]` adds `architecture`, both tests still pass, because each compares the code against its own table. AC-6 requires "every heading Key entities names for it", and AC-18 requires the decision table's rows.

`READERS["worker"]` written as `["stack"]`, or `HEADINGS["infra"]` and the infra template both missing `Eventing and queues`. The tests compare the output with the same table that produced it, so they pass.

say `READERS["worker"]` is built wrongly with `"architecture"` in it, or `HEADINGS["stack"]` and the stack template both leave out `CI`. Each pack or doc then matches the same wrong source, so TC-31 and TC-6 pass even though AC-18 (the decision table Docs per reader) and AC-6 (the headings Key entities names) are broken.

findings.reason: TC-6 compares each doc's headings with `onboard.HEADINGS[<doc>]`. Its only literal heading is `Commands`. TC-31 compares pack headings with `onboard.READERS[<r>]`. A wrong table entry in code (a missing `CI` heading, or `architecture` added to the worker's docs) would pass both tests.
findings.note: TC-6 and TC-31 assert literal headings and reader rows from the spec

findings.title: TC-44 can't catch a missing effort-close proposal or a missing dependency
quotes: Observable: proposal names stack.md and the dependency; stack.md bytes unchanged after a decline, holding the dependency after an approval.
- Assert: prints `pyproject.toml: stack.md`; stack.md bytes unchanged (nothing applied without the dev)
findings.fix: run `epic_done` on the fixture and assert the CT-20 line. Then cover the approval and the dependency name with an e2e test of the reconcile skill after an effort, or narrow AC-26 to what CT-11 and CT-20 do.

sources.situation: TC-44 covers CT-20 but never runs `flow.epic_done`, so a close that never prints the `project docs: ... changed` line passes. Nothing asserts that `httpx` (the dependency) is named, and the approval branch is not tested. "stack.md bytes unchanged" can't fail, because `onboard.changed` never writes.

`flow.epic_done` never prints the `project docs: ... propose edits with @nio:reconcile-onboarding` line, so when an effort finishes nothing is proposed. TC-44 still passes: it only calls `nio onboard changed` and `onboard.changed`. Its bytes check is true by construction, since neither call writes. The approval half of AC-26 is never tested.

findings.reason: TC-44 only runs `nio onboard changed` and `onboard.changed`, never `flow.epic_done`, so CT-20's printed line is untested. The only CT-20 test is TC-44, per the plan's Coverage table. It does not assert the dependency name. The "stack.md bytes unchanged" check cannot fail, because `onboard.changed` never writes.
findings.note: TC-44 asserts close_lines and the epic close line; dependency naming and apply/decline are reconcile's (TC-38, TC-41)

findings.title: TC-8 checks a line the test itself wrote, not one the agent wrote
quotes: - Setup: a repo with pyproject.toml; stack.md holding `- Python 3.12 (source: pyproject.toml@<h>)` where `<h>` is the hash `nio onboard scan` printed for it
Given a confirmed fact taken from pyproject.toml, when stack.md is written, then that fact names pyproject.toml and the file's hash at the time.
findings.fix: add to an existing onboard e2e test (for example TC-5) an assert that stack.md's fact lines carry `(source: pyproject.toml@<h>)` with `<h>` equal to the scan's hash.

sources.situation: AC-8 is about how stack.md gets written. If the onboard skill writes facts with no `(source: …)` record, or with a stale hash, TC-8 still passes, because its fixture line is hand-made. The asserts only show that `SOURCE` parses a well-formed record and that `stale` returns `[]`, which a stub returning `[]` also does.

findings.reason: TC-8's setup hand-writes the `(source: pyproject.toml@<h>)` line. TC-5, the e2e test that runs the skill and writes stack.md, asserts only that the framework is Flask and not Django. Nothing checks that the skill writes source records.
findings.note: TC-5 asserts Flask facts end with (source: pyproject.toml@<scan hash>)

findings.title: TC-30 sits before the drafting pack that gives the drafter the personas
quotes: the spec skill builds its drafting pack with `nio pack "<summary>" --reader spec`
- Delivers: CT-9, CT-10, CT-18, CT-19
findings.fix: move TC-30 to US-5, or have it build the drafter's input through `nio pack --reader spec`.

sources.situation: TC-30 is in US-4, but the `--reader spec` pack that puts personas.md in front of the drafter is CT-10 (with CT-9), delivered in US-5. In US-4 the drafter only sees personas if the test hands it the file directly. The test then passes without proving that the real pack carries personas, so a pack that drops personas.md goes unnoticed.

findings.reason: CT-16 makes the spec skill build its pack with `nio pack --reader spec`. CT-10 adds that flag and is delivered in US-5, but TC-30 sits in US-4. The test asserts nothing about the pack carrying personas.md.
findings.note: TC-30 moved to US-5, after the --reader spec pack exists

findings.title: The pack tests use `nio pack`, so the jury and worker wiring (CT-18, CT-19) goes untested
quotes: - Action: `nio pack "x" --reader <r>` for spec, scope, plan, architecture-fit and worker
appends `onboard.docs_for(root, "scope", slug)` to the scope lens's pack at the spec gate
memory, _ = pack.build(root, task["title"], task["files"], task["serves"], task["id"], worker=False)
findings.fix: add asserts that build a scope pack and an architecture-fit pack through `jury._pack_text`, and a worker pack through `implement.worker_pack`. Check each for its mapped `### ` headings, and check that the worker pack still has exactly five `## ` parts.

sources.situation: the jury's scope and architecture-fit packs are built by `jury._pack_text`, and a worker's pack by `implement.worker_pack`. Neither goes through `nio pack`. If `_pack_text` never calls `docs_for`, or `worker_pack` keeps calling `pack.build` without `reader="worker"`, every planned test still passes. Yet real lenses and workers get no project docs, which breaks AC-18 for the scope and architecture-fit lens readers and AC-35's worker pack.

every pack test goes through the `nio pack` CLI. Today `implement.worker_pack` calls `pack.build(root, task["title"], task["files"], task["serves"], task["id"], worker=False)` with no reader, and `jury._pack_text` is never called by any planned test. So a build where the real worker pack and the jury's scope and architecture-fit packs carry no project docs passes TC-31, TC-16 and TC-36. In the same way, `flow.epic_done` is never run, so a missing `project docs: … changed` line passes TC-44.

findings.reason: TC-31 (tests.md:226-231) and TC-16 drive every reader only through `nio pack`, while CT-18 binds `jury.py:_pack_text` and CT-19 binds `implement.py:worker_pack` (contracts.md:136-143). No planned test calls either function, so a build that leaves them without docs still passes.
findings.note: TC-31 drives jury._pack_text for scope and architecture-fit and implement.worker_pack (five parts kept); TC-44 runs the epic close

findings.title: TC-3's `.nio/` half can't fail: its fixture matches no category
quotes: - Setup: a repo whose .gitignore holds `build/`, with `build/README.md` and `.nio/project/notes.md`
product-docs `README*`, `docs/*.md`
keep a copy of the original at `.nio/backup/<date>/<path>`, which NIO never deletes and the scan never lists
findings.fix: use a `.nio/` fixture that matches a category, e.g. `.nio/backup/2026-11-08/CLAUDE.md` or `.nio/project/README.md`, and assert it is absent.

sources.situation: the scan drops its `.nio/` exclusion. `notes.md` matches no category pattern, so it is never listed anyway and TC-3 passes. Meanwhile `.nio/backup/<date>/CLAUDE.md` (agent-docs by base name) would be listed, against FR-3 and FR-29.

`notes.md` matches no category (no README*, no docs/*.md, no agent-docs name), so it is never listed whether or not the `.nio/` exclusion exists. If that exclusion is missing, `.nio/backup/<date>/CLAUDE.md` (written by FR-29) would be listed as agent-docs through the base-name match, and TC-3 still passes.

findings.reason: TC-3 (tests.md:33) uses `.nio/project/notes.md`, which matches none of the category patterns, so it is absent whether or not the `.nio/` exclusion exists. A `.nio/backup/<date>/CLAUDE.md` would be listed unnoticed.

- Assert: `nio status` prints no `stale:` line after the run
then stack.md is unchanged and records pyproject.toml's new hash
findings.fix: also assert the record is present with the new hash. For TC-41, `(source: pyproject.toml@<h>)` where `<h>` is the post-change hash from `nio onboard scan`. For TC-42, the same for CONTRIBUTING.md after the patch.

sources.situation: on a decline, reconcile deletes stack.md's `(source: pyproject.toml@…)` record rather than rewriting it. Or after the CONTRIBUTING.md patch, onboard never records CONTRIBUTING.md as a source of stack.md at all. In both cases nothing is left to go stale, so both tests pass while AC-42 and AC-43 fail.

suppose the reconcile skill, on a decline, strips the `(source: pyproject.toml@…)` record instead of writing the new hash. The text with records removed is then the same as before, and with no record `stale()` finds nothing. Both asserts pass while AC-42's "records pyproject.toml's new hash" is broken, and the fact silently loses its source.

findings.title: CT-18, CT-19 and CT-20 are never exercised by any test
quotes: - Action: `nio pack "x" --reader <r>` for spec, scope, plan, architecture-fit and worker
- Action: `nio pack "task" --reader worker --slug <slug>`
calls `pack.build(..., reader="worker", slug=slug)`, so the docs sit inside its first part and the pack keeps exactly five `## ` parts.
- Action: `nio onboard changed main`; and `onboard.changed(root, "main")`
findings.fix: add asserts that call `implement.worker_pack` (the docs are present and there are still exactly five `## ` parts) and `jury._pack_text` for scope and architecture-fit. For CT-20, run `flow.epic_done` on TC-44's fixture and assert the `project docs:` line.

sources.situation: every pack test goes through the `nio pack` CLI. Today `implement.worker_pack` calls `pack.build(root, task["title"], task["files"], task["serves"], task["id"], worker=False)` with no reader, and `jury._pack_text` is never called by any planned test. So a build where the real worker pack and the jury's scope and architecture-fit packs carry no project docs passes TC-31, TC-16 and TC-36. In the same way, `flow.epic_done` is never run, so a missing `project docs: … changed` line passes TC-44.
